# UFO Feel — Intake brief (final, producer answers incorporated)

**FINAL DRAFT** — producer answered Q1=B, Q2=C, Q3=A (see Appendix).
Stage to follow: intake_complete (via intake finish + coverage review).

## Problem statement

The Mystery UFO collector drone flies, harvests and dies **silently and
without feedback**: it has no visual effects and no sounds for any lifecycle
moment, so the reward reads as dead game feel. We need the classic Space
Invaders mystery-ship juice: a "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble while it is deployed,
a reward cue when it returns to the player, and an explosion plus a "tinkle" of
dropped resources when it is destroyed — with full-juice VFX at every lifecycle
stage.

## Users

- **Player** (the primary stakeholder) — wants the Mystery UFO to *feel* like
  the Space Invaders homage it is: an audible, celebratory arcade reward with
  visible juice at spawn, on collect, on return and on death.
- **Developer / quality gates** — wants the juice to run through the existing
  ToneForge audio pipeline and shared VFX so the game and every gym stay
  identical (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole
  sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.
- As a player, I want to see the saucer come alive (running-light pulse, a poof
  on launch, sparkles as it vacuums, a trail on the way home) so the drone
  reads as a living reward.
- As a player, I want a reward fanfare when the drone flies home and pays out
  so the economic payoff feels earned.
- As a player, I want a satisfying explosion and the tinkle of minerals
  scattering when an enemy shoots the drone down, so the loss/opportunity
  reads clearly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Warble loop (Q2=C).** A classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays continuously from spawn through the **seek and collect** phases (the whole sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
2. **Reward cue (Q3=A).** A distinct reward fanfare plays on **arrival at the player**, synchronised with the hold pay-in (exactly when `MysteryUfoDrone._payOut` credits the sink), so the payout moment is audible.
3. **Destruction feedback.** On enemy destruction the drone plays an explosion cue **and** spawns the explosion particle VFX at the crash site (reusing `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`); a mineral "tinkle" cue fires in sync with the spilled resource drops (spill already exists via `hitDrone`/`scatterMineralDrops`), so the dropped minerals read audibly.
4. **Full-juice VFX (Q1=B).** Code-drawn Phaser graphics (no external art) add the full lifecycle juice: spawn poof at launch, per-mineral collect sparkle/ring while vacuuming, a running-light pulse animation on the saucer rim, and a return-leg trail/glow — all in addition to the destruction explosion VFX.
5. **Pipeline, parity & quality.** Every new cue is a baked ToneForge delivery (recipe YAMLs under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, entries in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, wrappers in `src/audio/effects.ts`, WAVs rendered via `npm run build-audio`); the cue-manifest / effects-contract / build-audio / audio-balance-guard suites pass; the continuous warble has start/stop control lifecycle and every cue degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext; the VFX/SFX run through shared core so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes are identical (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion pass, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` green); the full project test suite passes and relevant docs (GDD §7.3 / Mystery UFO section, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`) are updated.

## Constraints

- Audio must flow through the existing ToneForge pipeline — no new external
  assets (procedural WAV baked at build time; `file:../ToneForge` dependency).
- The continuous warble requires start/stop control lifecycle (`ControlCues` in
  the manifest) and must respect the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
- VFX must be code-drawn Phaser graphics (repo convention: no external art).
- Every cue must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests and
  autoplay-blocked browsers) — the effects contract suite enforces this.
- Behaviour must live once in shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and be consumed
  by both the game and the gyms (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- Peak-volume/balance guarded by `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs`.

## Existing state

- `MysteryUfoDrone` (src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts) is a pure entity with a
  code-drawn saucer (running lights, dome, glow) but **zero VFX/SFX**: no cue is
  called anywhere in the drone, the shared pass (`src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`),
  or the spawn path. Collection (`_vacuum`) hides minerals with no feedback;
  destruction (`_destroyByEnemy` + `hitDrone`) already spills minerals via
  `scatterMineralDrops` but with no explosion/tinkle feedback.
- The audio pipeline is ToneForge-baked: `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps
  every cue to a recipe; `src/audio/effects.ts` exports thin playback wrappers;
  WAVs are baked by `npm run build-audio`. No UFO cue exists yet.

## Desired change

Add the "feel" layer so every Mystery UFO lifecycle moment gives feedback
through the shared pipeline, identically in the game and the gyms: warble for
the whole sortie, a reward fanfare on payout, explosion + mineral tinkle +
particle burst on destruction, plus the full-juice VFX set (spawn poof, collect
sparkle, running-light pulse, return trail).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — lifecycle state hooks (spawn, collect,
  return, payout, destroyed) driving the SFX/VFX seams; running-light pulse
  animation in the saucer draw/update.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` — shared tick/spawn/destroy pass: warble
  start/stop in `tickDrones`, destruction explosion + tinkle adjacent to the
  existing spill in `hitDrone`, spawn poof in `spawnDrone`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` /
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shared wiring so game and gyms run the same code.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue wrappers: warble loop + `stopMysteryUfoWarbleSound`
  control companion, `playMysteryUfoRewardSound`, `playMysteryUfoDestroySound`,
  `playMineralTinkleSound`.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue→recipe entries (+ control cue).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — new `aihell-mystery-ufo-*` recipes
  (warble, reward, destroy, mineral tinkle).
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` / `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`
  — continuous-cue start/stop plumbing for the warble.
- `src/vfx/` — spawn poof, collect sparkle/ring, return trail (small new/module
  effects, following `explosionParticles.ts` conventions); `explosionParticles.ts`
  reused for the destruction burst.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§7.3 + Mystery UFO section),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G113S009B37I** — Mystery UFO has no visible representation (epic,
  completed): the collector-drone entity and shared pass this item adds feel to.
- **AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92** — Mystery UFO needs a better graphical representation
  (completed): the code-drawn saucer VFX baseline this item animates.
- **AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7** — Space Invaders mystery UFO bonus (completed): the
  classic reference the warble/reward homage draws from.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J** — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge (epic): the pipeline every new cue must flow through.
- **AH-0MVBMPZ2C0008VAE** — Drone level variables and curve specs (completed).
- **AH-0MVBMQ0HR0064THH** — Gym parity for the collector drone (completed).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **VFX scope.** "The item says the Mystery UFO currently has no VFX or
  SFX but does not specify which visual effects to add. (a) Minimal...; (b)
  Full juice — also add spawn poof, return-trail/glow, running-light pulse;
  (c) Sound-only."
  — Answer (producer, via review reply "1. B (with SFX)"): **B — full juice**,
  with the SFX set confirmed in scope alongside the VFX. Source: producer
  review reply on AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6 (comment thread
  AH-C0MVNZ64M5000W4NL). Final AC 4 (full-juice VFX) + ACs 1–3 (SFX) reflect
  this.
- Q2: **"woo-woo-woo" delivery.** "(a) continuous looping cue while the drone
  is in the collect phase; (b) discrete one-shot per collected mineral; (c) a
  looping cue that plays for the whole sortie (seek+collect)."
  — Answer (producer, "2. C"): **C — loop for the whole sortie** (seek +
  collect), so the warble starts at spawn and ends at return/payout/destruction.
  Source: producer review reply. Final AC 1 reflects this.
- Q3: **Reward timing.** "(a) on arrival at the ship, synchronised with the
  payout pay-in; (b) when the drone begins the return leg; (c) both."
  — Answer (producer, "3. A"): **A — on arrival/payout**, synced with the hold
  credit. Source: producer review reply. Final AC 2 reflects this.

### Assumptions (documented)

- The original description's "no VFX or VFX" is a typo for "no VFX or SFX"
  (confirmed implicitly by Q1 answer B *with SFX*).
- Level progression (lifetime/capacity/radius) does **not** change the sound
  character — same cues at every level (no per-level variant recipes).
- New cues respect the existing volume balance budget (≤ ~0.2 peak per layer,
  `audio-balance-guard`) and the global SFX mute/volume settings automatically
  via the shared playback provider.
- Running-light pulse is a static-free animation of the existing
  code-drawn lights (alpha/colour oscillation), not a new emitter.

### Risks

- **Audio-pipeline risk (med).** Every new cue is a build-time WAV bake: recipe
  YAML, manifest entry, wrapper and `npm run build-audio` render must stay in
  lock-step or the contract suites (cue-manifest / effects-contract /
  build-audio / audio-balance-guard) fail red. Mitigation: follow the exact
  pattern of an existing baked cue (e.g. `aihell-diver-dive-loop`) end to end.
- **Continuous-cue lifecycle risk (med).** The sortie-long warble must start
  exactly once at spawn and stop on every terminal path (return, payout,
  destroyed, teardown) or it will leak a looping voice. Mitigation: start/stop
  via the shared control-companion pattern (`ControlCues`) and asset in
  `tickDrones` where removal is final; extend the cue-contract test to assert
  stop-on-all-terminals.
- **Collect-sparkle VFX performance (low-med).** At the max collector radius
  (40 px) a drone can vacuum several minerals in one tick; a sparkle per
  mineral must be small, short-lived and capped, not an unbounded emitter.
  Mitigation: reuse `explosionParticles`-style pooled graphics and cap per-tick
  spawns.
- **Parity risk (med).** If a gym or `PlayScene` wires the SFX/VFX outside the
  shared core, the duplicate-body guard / gym-parity docs assertion fail and
  the game and gyms drift. Mitigation: implement through
  `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` and shared hooks only (AGENTS.md
  architecture convention).
- **Scope-creep risk (med).** The chosen full-juice VFX set (poof, sparkle,
  pulse, trail) is wide for one item. Extra polish discovered during
  implementation (e.g. pay-in burst on the ship, level-scaled bloom) must be
  recorded as new work items, not absorbed into this one.

### Duplicate-work check

Performed `wl search "UFO"` / `"woo"` / `"mystery ufo vfx"` — completed items
cover visual representation (AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92), visibility epic
(AH-0MV9G113S009B37I) and the classic reference (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7); **no
overlapping item for UFO audio/VFX feel exists**. No duplicate — proceed.
---

## Plan: changelog (plan skill, AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6)

- **2026-10-28** — Planned via /skill:plan. Pre-check `plan-if-needed` → `plan` (Small/Medium); plan-approval-gate → `request_approval: false` (no approval pause). Created 6 child items (test-first): UFO feel test seams, ToneForge UFO cue bake, Sortie warble lifecycle, Terminal reward and destruction feedback, Saucer lifecycle VFX juice, UFO feel docs and quality gate. Deps wired (test seams + cue bake → warble → terminal feedback; VFX → docs/gate). Parent AC section unwrapped to single lines so AC coverage is machine-comparable (formatting only). Six automated review stages run; AC coverage review → `proceed` (all 5 parent ACs covered). Parent stage → `plan_complete`. Effort/risk reused from existing estimate (Small / Medium, comment AH-C0MVNZHO3W000ZBLP) — not re-estimated.

### Appendix addition (planning run)

- Q: "Did planning need any further clarifying questions from the producer?" — Answer (this run): No new questions. All three design decisions were already resolved in intake (Q1=B full juice, Q2=C whole-sortie warble, Q3=A arrival/payout, recorded above), the effort/risk estimate is on file, and the plan-approval gate requested no approval. Planning proceeded from the intake brief's Acceptance Criteria directly.

# Intake Brief — Waves need more variation in enemy types

**Headline:** Make all 100 campaign waves draw from a wider enemy-type mix so no two sequential waves share the same enemy composition, while preserving each level's dominant-archetype identity and the existing difficulty ramp, fire boundary and determinism contract.

## Seed description

> Waves within a level should show more variation in enemy types.

## Problem statement

The shipped 10 × 10 campaign (100 waves) reads as repetitive within each level: Level 1 is Scout-only across all ten waves, Level 5 is Phaser-only, and the `fixed` filler waves in Levels 1–3 and the `fixed` showcases throughout are hand-authored compositions reused verbatim. Only L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 are `dynamic`. Within-level enemy-type variety is therefore the exception rather than the rule, and a player experiences long runs of the same enemies (e.g. ten Scout waves in a row at the start of the run).

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want each wave in a level to field different enemy types from the preceding wave, so the campaign feels varied rather than monotonous across a run.
- **As a player**, I want each level to keep a recognisable identity (its dominant archetype), so the onboarding ramp and the "Predictable Death" pattern-testing level stay legible.
- **As a designer**, I want the variation enforced as a campaign-wide invariant (not per-level hand-tuning), so future wave edits cannot silently reintroduce sequential repetition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No sequential repetition.** No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition. *Verification:* unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config; applies to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **AC2 — Whole-campaign coverage.** All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves. *Verification:* per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **AC3 — Level identity preserved.** Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying *around* it with secondary archetypes. *Verification:* per-level dominant-archetype assertions; GDD §3.2 identity text still holds.
- **AC4 — Balance rules respected.** Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix). *Verification:* existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests still pass over the rebuilt campaign.
- **AC5 — No regression of difficulty ramp and boundaries.** The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary, and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass. *Verification:* existing campaign regression and invariant suites.
- **AC6 — Determinism and reproducibility.** Same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent, `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed). *Verification:* seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New or updated unit/integration tests cover sequential distinctness, per-level identity, determinism and regression; **the full project test suite passes with the new changes**.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `README.md`, the GDD (§3.2 level descriptions and the default-campaign note), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any relevant docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B): re-mix the 18-archetype roster (`scout`, `diver`, `tank`, `phaser`, `swarm`, `boss`, `asteroid`, `harvester`, `march`, `capturer`, `ghost-chase`, `ghost-ambush`, `ghost-flank`, `ghost-wander`, `grunt`, `raider`, `lane-traffic`, `orbital-strike`); do not invent new archetypes unless the producer explicitly requests them.
- **"Same enemies"** is interpreted as the same set of enemy archetypes in a wave's composition (order/spacing/count variations alone are not "different enemies"). The sequential-distinctness rule applies to generated waves as well (producer Q3 = c').
- **Level identity (Q2 = a):** the dominant archetype of each level is preserved; variety is added around it.
- **Mixed mechanism (Q3 = c'):** hand-authored `fixed` waves stay where a specific showcase/pin is required (wave-10 mini-bosses, classic-arcade debuts, L1 onboarding pin); `curve` waves stay deterministic; filler waves that are currently `fixed` may move to `dynamic` where safe, seeded per-run under R1–R3 guardrails.
- **Determinism contract** (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT): `curve`/`fixed` seed-independent; `dynamic` pure function of (curve, pool, seed).
- **Fire boundary** (GDD §2.4/§2.5): Levels 1–3 do not fire; Levels 4–10 do. Generated waves derive fire rules from level number.
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): wave data/logic live in the shared core consumed by both `PlayScene` and the gyms; any divergence must be justified and recorded.
- **No target-curve re-tuning unless required** to satisfy AC1–AC3; if the ramp must move to break sequential repetition, it stays within the no-degeneracy + non-decreasing + strictly-rising aggregated difficulty constraints.
- **UK English** in all code comments, tests and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — 100 rows; L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2 `dynamic`; most other L1–L3 rows `fixed`; L5W2 `dynamic`; Level 4+ mixed `curve`/`fixed`; wave 10 of every level `fixed` mini-boss.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` hand-authored waves (used for `fixed`); Level 1 all Scout V-formations; Level 5 Phaser-only; classic-arcade showcases on Levels 6–10.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS`, `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`, `defaultDifficultyCurves()`; per-wave mode overrides supported (`DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES[level]?.[wave]`).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-wave `generation` dispatch (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`); `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` for openings; seeded dynamic jitter.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — runtime auto-sequencer; `defaultCandidatePool()`; composition from `enemyDifficulty` targets.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — pure R1–R3 rules + validator (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP); generator hard-constraints.
- Tests: `waveBalance.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `sequencedLevels.test.ts` (incl. "Retuned default campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K)" and phaser-only filler pins), `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 (L1 Scout V-formations).

## Desired change

- Extend enemy-type variety across all 100 waves so sequential waves differ in composition, per level identity (Q2 = a) and via the mixed fixed/curve/dynamic mechanism (Q3 = c').
- Introduce a campaign-wide sequential-distinctness invariant (producer Q1 = a + explicit rule), enforced in the shared builder/sequencer and tested.
- Keep hand-authored `fixed` waves where showcase/pin/identity requires; relax only what is needed to satisfy AC1–AC2.
- Where safe, convert currently-`fixed` filler waves to `dynamic` (seeded per-run variety) under the balance-rule guardrails; otherwise extend the authored `LEVELS` data to mix secondary archetypes into identity waves.
- Update documentation (GDD §3.2 level wording, default-campaign note, enemy-design docs, README, code comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — per-wave `generation` mode changes; possible minor target retunes for AC1–AC2.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — add secondary archetypes to identity-preserving `fixed` waves; keep showcases/mini-bosses.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — sequential-distinctness enforcement seam; possibly broaden `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION`-style curation to filler waves.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — composition constraint for sequential distinctness if enforced in the sequencer; pool/jitter tuning.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — reuse R1–R3 validator for sequential-distinctness auditing (additive rule/named constant if needed).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES` updates if filler waves move to `dynamic`.
- Tests — `sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts` (or new `campaignVariety.test.ts`), `WaveManager.test.ts`, `configStore.test.ts`, `csv-seed.test.ts`.
- Docs — `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2 + default-campaign note, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B** — Create more variety in the first 3-4 waves (completed v0.1.9): made L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic`; the partial-overlap precedent this item extends to all 100 waves.
- **AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP** — Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling (completed v0.1.13): R1–R3 rules + validator; must keep passing (AC4).
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed): the ramp/regression pins AC5 preserves.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed): the mode dispatch + determinism contract.
- **AH-0MVCYANT6003SG5C / AH-0MVCRAR89009C8GZ** — 10-wave campaign data foundation + re-land (completed v0.1.14): the 100-wave grid this item varies.
- **AH-0MV398ZWL009TTOB** — Write campaign-level invariant tests (completed): precedent for campaign-wide invariants.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — identity vs sequential-distinctness tension (high).** Level 1 (Scout) and Level 5 (Phaser) must keep a dominant archetype yet not repeat across ten waves. *Mitigation:* allow 2–3 archetypes per level with the dominant sharing the most waves; assert "≥ 2 archetypes per level" plus "no adjacent identical composition", not "all ten waves distinct types".
- **Risk — ramp/regression disturbance (medium).** Re-mixing archetypes can shift `targetDifficulty` fit. *Mitigation:* reuse the retuned targets; retune only within the no-degeneracy/non-decreasing/strictly-rising constraints if required; keep the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins green.
- **Risk — sequencer target misses under a distinctness constraint (medium).** Enforcing "different archetype set from the previous wave" in `curve`/`dynamic` generation can push some waves off their `targetDifficulty` or shrink the candidate space. *Mitigation:* bias the sequencer towards the previous wave's complement (rules may trade exact target match for distinctness, following the R1–R3 precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP), or hand-author that wave as `fixed`; record resulting target error in the balance audit.
- **Risk — scope creep.** New archetypes, per-wave special mechanics, or reworking mini-bosses are out of scope; record as linked work items.
- **Assumption — existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B); no new archetypes unless the producer requests them.
- **Assumption — "same enemies" = same archetype set** in a wave's composition; count/order/spacing changes do not count as distinct.
- **Assumption — Q3 = c'** reads as the recommended mixed mechanism (authored `fixed` where pinned; `dynamic` for filler where safe), with the sequential-distinctness rule binding on generated waves too. If the producer intended otherwise, the mechanism sections of this brief change but AC1–AC3, AC5–AC8 stand.
- **Assumption — the sequential-distinctness rule is cross-wave, not cross-level** ("sequential within a level"); a wave-10 mini-boss and the next level's wave 1 are different levels and are not compared.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope — which waves need more enemy-type variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ88SK007XAFJ): **(a)** all 100 campaign waves, **plus the explicit rule: no two sequential waves should have the same enemies**. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Level identities — should the deliberate single-type levels stay pure?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8CBE00748J3): **(a)** preserve each level's dominant archetype/identity but add variety around it. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q3: "Mechanism — deterministic authored waves or seeded dynamic per-run variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8FVZ005AERQ): **(c')** mixed, as in the recommended (c); the sequential-distinctness constraint applies to generated waves too. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Research (agent): current campaign state audited (10 × 10 grid, mode ledger per wave); Level 1 Scout-only and Level 5 Phaser-only identities pinned by GDD §3.2/§2.5 and by `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 / `sequencedLevels.test.ts` phaser-only pins; duplicate check performed (partial overlap only with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B). Source: repo inspection + worklog search, this session (comments AH-C0MVNZ7UJ1005DJ9V).

## Related work (automated report)

_Appended after the find-related skill run (step 7)._

## Plan: feature decomposition

Decomposed into nine child work items following a **test-first, three-phase vertical-slice** cadence. Each phase cuts through data, code, tests and comments; the next phase's item descriptions are reviewed after each phase lands.

### Phase A — measure, then pilot the hardest case

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Campaign variety audit + failing invariants (AH-0MVSE6D2L0034SKG) | feature | Shared pure module `waveComposition` / `auditCampaignVariety` / `LEVEL_IDENTITY` + staged campaign assertions and the red-baseline audit snapshot |
| A2 | Relax single-type pins to identity-preserving (AH-0MVSE6F0O00689TT) | task | Convert "scouts only" / "phasers only" pins into dominance assertions (Q2=a) |
| A3 | Level 1 + Level 5 pilot: identity-preserving variety (AH-0MVSE6VIW009QG2E) | feature | Tracer bullet on the two highest-risk identity levels |

### Phase B — enforce, then rework the campaign

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Enforce sequential distinctness for generated waves (AH-0MVSE6XIO007BXYM) | feature | Seeded-deterministic constraint on `curve`/`dynamic` waves, R1–R3 precedence preserved |
| B2 | Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding) (AH-0MVSE7F090010EG3) | feature | Re-mix the no-fire onboarding `fixed` waves |

| B4 | Document and verify the fixed/curve/dynamic mode mix (AH-0MVSE7GWU0074H5I) | task | Explicit mode ledger + drift test (Q3=c'); conversion only where authored data cannot express intent |

### Phase C — prove and document

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Campaign variety regression, determinism and full-suite verification (AH-0MVSE7ILL000Y27B) | task | AC1–AC7 evidence, seed sweep, gym↔game parity, full suite |
| C2 | Documentation for campaign enemy-type variety (AH-0MVSE7KGQ002L2E2) | docs | GDD §3.2 + default-campaign note, enemy-design invariant section, README |

**Dependency order** (enforced with `wl dep`): A1 → A2 → A3 → B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → C1 → C2. A3 and B1 could run in parallel but are serialised because both touch the shared wave modules.

### Key design decisions recorded during planning

- **"Same enemies" = same archetype set**, counting wave groups **and** spawner opt-in flags (ghosts, centipede, horde, lane-traffic). Count/order/spacing changes alone do not satisfy AC1 — so re-tuning counts cannot fake variety.
- **Scope reality check:** only 12 of the 100 waves are currently generated (`curve`/`dynamic`); the other 88 are authored `fixed` waves reused verbatim from `LEVELS`. The dominant work is therefore authored data (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), not the sequencer. The sequencer still needs the distinctness constraint because AC1 binds on generated waves too.
- **Test-first without a red commit:** the audit module and its unit tests land green (A1) along with the recorded red-baseline snapshot; each campaign-wide assertion is *activated* by the item that makes it green, so the repo's never-commit-red rule is respected while the test-first intent is preserved.
- **Dominance, not purity:** D1 of the risk register (identity vs distinctness) is resolved by asserting dominant archetype + ≥ 2 archetypes per level + no adjacent duplicates — never "all ten waves distinct archetypes".
- **Rules win over distinctness:** R1–R3 keep precedence, matching the existing precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP; a wave that cannot meet distinctness inside the acceptance band becomes authored `fixed` data instead of widening the band.
- **No public API break:** `buildSequencedLevels(rows, candidates)` keeps working; the new controls are optional fields.

## Plan: vertical-slice verification

Each phase is a vertical slice, not a horizontal layer:

- **Phase A** delivers, in one green increment: the shared analysis code, its unit tests, the identity-pin contract, the authored Level 1/Level 5 data, the palette of comments and the audit report — proving the pattern end-to-end on the two hardest levels.
- **Phase B** delivers the generated-wave constraint plus the remaining authored data plus the mode ledger, each with its own tests and comments, keeping the whole campaign green at each step.
- **Phase C** delivers verification evidence and the documentation contract.

Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated with what the previous phase learned (recorded as comments on the parent). No phase is a horizontal "all tests then all code" split.

AC coverage review: `proceed` (8/8 parent ACs covered).

Idempotent revision record — appended by the plan session; the intake appendix above is unchanged and remains authoritative for the producer's decisions.

- **No new clarifying questions were needed.** The three blocking product decisions were answered at intake (Q1 = a + sequential-distinctness rule; Q2 = a dominant-archetype identity; Q3 = c' mixed mechanism with the constraint binding on generated waves), and every remaining planning input was resolvable from the repository. Re-asking them would have violated the shared interview contract's "do not ask questions already answered" rule.
- **Q1 (scope) — reused from intake.** Answer: all 100 campaign waves plus the explicit rule that no two sequential waves share the same enemies. Evidence: intake appendix, comment AH-C0MVNZ88SK007XAFJ (producer, interactive round 1). Planning consequence: AC1 is implemented as a campaign-wide invariant covering `curve`, `dynamic` **and** `fixed` modes, and the bulk of the work is authored `LEVELS` data (88 of 100 waves are `fixed`).
- **Q2 (level identity) — reused from intake.** Answer: preserve each level's dominant archetype and add variety around it. Evidence: comment AH-C0MVNZ8CBE00748J3. Planning consequence: purity pins become dominance pins (child A2); `LEVEL_IDENTITY` becomes the single source of truth (child A1) shared by tests and docs.
- **Q3 (mechanism) — reused from intake.** Answer: c' — mixed; authored `fixed` where a showcase/pin requires it, generated where safe, with the distinctness rule binding on generated waves too. Evidence: comment AH-C0MVNZ8FVZ005AERQ. Planning consequence: child B1 (generated distinctness) + child B4 (explicit mode ledger) rather than wholesale conversion of waves to `dynamic`.
- **Research (agent).** Repository inspection established the concrete starting state: 10 × 10 grid; per-wave modes from `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (L1W1/L1W2/L2W1/L2W2 `dynamic`; L5W2 `dynamic`; L4 W1–3, L5 W1, L6 W3–4, L7 W3–4, L9 W3, L10 W2 `curve`; the remaining 88 waves `fixed`); static `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts` supplies those `fixed` waves verbatim; `MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL = 1` caps a generated archetype to one wave per level; `waveBalance` R1–R3 validator is the shared rule module. # Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.
3. The journal path is git-ignored so a crashed run leaves no worktree change, asserted by a .gitignore guard test.
4. A deterministic, documented repair path restores the CSV exactly, documented in docs/BALANCING.md together with the journal file name.
5. Unit tests cover the journal write, restore-from-journal and stale-journal reconciliation, run under the project test policy (test skill).
6. Existing tune behaviour is preserved: --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore, exits 0, and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.

# Build Candidate D — Hangar War (the outer loop)

Follow-on to **We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)**, whose deliverable
(`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`) the producer reviewed and closed by choosing
**Candidate D — Hangar War** on 2026-10-29 (`discovered-from:AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC`).
This item turns that chosen design into a playable, shippable build. The design
rationale, comparison and the agreed adjustments live in
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D) and GDD §8; they are the
requirements of record for this item.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want my runs to add up to a war I can win — a hangar worth
defending, a ring of hexes around it, and weapons I discover by beating the bosses
that wield them — so that losing a run costs me a ship and its salvage, not my
progress, and so that "beating the boss" is a milestone on the way to holding the
ring rather than the end of everything.

As the producer, I want Candidate D shipped in the order the design recommends —
**Candidate B's MVP (hangar economy) first, then the first hex ring** — so that if
the ring disappoints in play, the hangar stands alone as a complete outer loop and
no work is wasted.

## Scope (from the chosen design)

**Two outer-loop progression axes running together:**
1. **The war on the map** — a hex grid whose first **ring of six hexes** surrounds
   the hangar; which hexes are held, which hold a defending bot, and how aggressive
   the frontier is.
2. **The range of the fleet** — the hangar: hulls, starting weapons, loadouts and
   permanent modifiers bought with banked salvage.

**The capture cycle:** attack a **weak** neighbouring hex → collect salvage →
defeat its **boss** → receive a **new kind of power-up or weapon** into the hangar
→ **leave a bot** flying one of your hulls to defend the hex.

**The frontier:** between runs the AI's border aggression rises and it can
**retake** a held hex unless the player defeats the attacking neighbour. A lost
*run* is still final (ship and unbanked salvage gone); the hangar never is.
Hex defence, mineral accrual and the aggression tick are **algorithmic
resolutions over stored strength numbers** — no live simulated battle.

**Entry surface (producer decision 2026-10-30, Q1 = a):** the hangar war is
reached from its **own top-level menu entry**; **Play Game keeps running the
shipped classic campaign** exactly as today and **Continue — Level N keeps
resuming the arcade run checkpoint**. The two modes share the run code
(`PlayScene` + shared core) but never share session or checkpoint state — a
hex deployment cannot overwrite the arcade checkpoint, and vice versa.

## Agreed design adjustments (2026-10-29 producer review — requirements)

1. **Ring timing is an evening's play, not a grind.** MVP (one ring, six hexes)
   targets **40–60 minutes** for a semi-skilled player: 6 × ≈5-minute
   deployments (≈30 min) plus build/salvage time and a few losses. **Ring 2 is
   larger — 12 hexes**, ≈60 minutes of deployments plus 10–40 minutes of builds
   and losses (~70–100 min). Later rings grow again (ring *n* holds 6*n* hexes),
   so the campaign gets progressively longer, not repetitive.
2. **Boss and weapon strengths are known ahead (MVP).** Before committing to a
   hex the player can see what its boss is, what it is strong/weak against, and
   which hex grants which weapon — enabling deliberate strategy ("take that hex → I
   get the weapon that counters the boss threatening my home hex"). Going beyond
   strategic weapon grants is **out of scope for the MVP**; it is the backlog below.
3. **One hex holds the new weapon — and it is the hardest in the ring.** The other
   five hexes grant upgrades/strength. Players may rush the hard hex and push into
   the next ring (risking losses) or grind the weaker hexes and secure the ring
   first — **different play styles must all be viable** (strategists, grinders,
   completers).
4. **Starting kit clarification.** The *fleet* starts minimal (one basic hull, one
   starting weapon, no hangar modifiers), but the *run* keeps the shipped middle
   loop in full: the six shared loadout slots (any mix of power-up and weapon
   kinds) plus the two slot-free kinds, **Extra Life** and **Mystery UFO**. Do not
   strip the shipped in-run variety to create the outer loop's scarcity.
5. **Post-MVP mitigation backlog (design captured, not MVP):** special missions
   with special rewards (e.g. a new hull type with extra hit points or extra
   upgrade bays), upgraded bots with special skills that are more effective
   against certain enemy/boss types, and further variety so the ring is never a
   six-chore checklist.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hangar slice first (Candidate B's MVP).** Banked salvage (minerals + mini-boss
   cores at the existing checkpoint moments), a persistent hangar with one extra
   hull, three unlockable starting weapons, one permanent modifier, and a
   deployment/loadout selector; losing a run forfeits only that run's unbanked
   salvage.
2. **One hex ring.** A hex-grid map screen with the hangar at the centre and a ring
   of six hexes, each showing held/unheld, aggression, its boss, its granted
   weapon/upgrade and any pending attack; ring growth is data-driven **and ring 2
   (12 hexes) is playable in this build**, generated from hex definitions
   (producer decision 2026-10-30, Q3 = a).
3. **Capture cycle.** Taking a hex = a normal run at that hex's aggression, ending
   in the hex boss; defeating the boss banks salvage, grants the hex's weapon or
   upgrade into the hangar, and lets the player leave a bot flying a chosen hull.
   **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held** (producer decision
   2026-10-30, Q2 = a); the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state
   are deferred, see *Out of scope*.
4. **Algorithmic defence + frontier tick.** A pure resolver decides holds/falls from
   stored numbers (defender rating vs attacking force × aggression); one frontier
   tick between runs raises border aggression and can retake a hex; the defence
   report shows the numbers that produced every result.
5. **Boss-granted discovery.** A hex boss demonstrates the weapon it grants; the
   entry appears in the hangar only after the boss is defeated (Rule 2), with the
   six-slot, Extra Life and Mystery UFO behaviour of the shipped run unchanged
   (Rule 1 clarification).
6. **Known-ahead intel, visible.** Hex bosses, their weaknesses and the weapon each
   hex grants are readable before the player commits to a deployment.
7. **Timing targets.** One-ring MVP is completable in 40–60 minutes by a
   semi-skilled player; ring 2 (12 hexes) lands at ≈70–100 minutes; the timing is
   recorded in the GDD and measured with the headless eval arena
   (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` per-run durations, summed per ring).
8. **Playstyles supported.** A rush through the weapon hex into the next ring, and a
   full grind of the ring before pushing, are both viable and neither is strictly
   dominant; the difficulty curve makes the aggressive line riskier but faster.
9. **Gym coverage and parity.** Hangar economy, defence resolver and frontier clock
   ship as pure logic exercised in a `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` scene; any new hull,
   weapon or bot behaviour runs the **same code** in gym and game (AGENTS.md
   gym↔game parity, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated).
10. **Attract mode never stalls.** The demo bot traverses or skips the map, hangar
    and defence report (auto-pick weakest hex, auto-buy cheapest useful unlock) and
    there is no live defence battle to stall in.
11. **Persistence.** One versioned `localStorage` key for hangar + ring under GDD
    §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend, injectable store), with a migration
    note; a partial ring is never discarded.
12. **Additive entry surface.** The main menu gains a **Hangar War** entry;
    **Play Game still starts the shipped classic 10-level campaign** and
    **Continue — Level N still resumes the arcade run checkpoint**, with no
    shared session state between the modes (producer decision 2026-10-30,
    Q1 = a).
13. **Build and full suite green**, and the docs/code comments updated.

## Out of scope

- Candidate A's region graph, faction simulation and home-world search; Candidates
  B and C as separate builds (B's MVP is the first slice of this item).
- Post-MVP mitigations beyond known-ahead intel (special missions, upgraded bots) —
  design captured in the candidates document, scheduled later.
- **The ring's massed counter-attack on the hangar and the hangar-falls lose
  state.** Deferred by producer decision (2026-10-30, Q2 = a): the MVP's ring
  win is "all six hexes held". Tracked for later by **AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK**.
- Any backend, or a real-time (simulated) hex defence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — extend or sit alongside for the outer-loop payload.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — reuse (scores, hex aggression → curve).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/` — deployment entry, no divergent copy.
- new: hangar/hex map scenes, `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar`, pure resolver + frontier clock modules and their tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md`.

## Dependencies

- Builds on the completed design deliverable AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC (chosen Candidate D).
- Overlaps the attract-bot framework AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4 (traversal requirement) and the checkpoint save/resume AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51 (persistence precedent).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** Candidate D's design decisions of record are the ones recorded in
  AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC's AC16 record and GDD §8; changing them is a producer call.
- **Risk — the frontier treadmill:** AI retakes hexes faster than a casual player can
  hold them. Mitigation: every tick is answerable, and the numbers are shown.
- **Risk — two progressions, twice the bookkeeping.** Mitigation: one screen holds
  map and hangar, one click apart.
- **Risk — power creep** trivialises hexes; mitigation: ring depth raises difficulty
  and each weapon arrives only after being beaten.

## Existing state (repository survey, dev @ `0787ab6a`)

- **No outer-loop code exists yet.** A repo-wide search of `src/` for
  `hangar`, `hexGrid`, `HexRing` and salvage banking finds **nothing in
  production code** — Candidate D is design-only today
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D, GDD §8). Nothing but the
  conventions below constrains the new modules' shape.
- **Persistence precedents to copy, not reinvent:** `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`
  (v2 payload, `CHECKPOINT_STORAGE_KEY`, injectable `CheckpointStorage`,
  defensive parse → `null`, field-presence migration),
  `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/core/settingsStore.ts` and
  `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` (versioned corrupt-safe blob with a bundled
  baseline). GDD §6.6 lists the shipped keys (`ai_hell_leaderboard`,
  `ai_hell_settings`, `ai_hell_checkpoint`, `ai_hell_lastSession`); the outer
  loop's `ai_hell_hangar_war` is a fifth key under the same rules.
- **Difficulty reuse:** `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is consumed through
  `src/core/difficultyScaling.ts`, `difficultySequencer.ts` and
  `levelScaling.ts`; a hex's aggression should select/perturb those curves
  rather than introduce a second scaling system.
- **Entry surface:** `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` exposes Play Game,
  Continue — Level N (only when a usable checkpoint exists), Leaderboard,
  Settings, Help and the dev-only Gym Scene Index. There is **no mode
  selector** today, and Play Game deliberately clears the checkpoint.
- **Gym surface:** 14 scenes under `src/scenes/gym/` plus the generic
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, registered in `GymIndex`.
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` fails if a gym scene has no row in
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` pins
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, so two new gym scenes imply updates to both.
- **Attract bot:** `src/ai/` (botDecision, botSnapshot, botHumanLike,
  framework/competent, eval arena) and `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`
  exist, but the demo boots straight into `PlayScene` — **no scene-to-scene
  menu traversal is shipped today**, so AC10 is new behaviour rather than a
  reuse.
- **Timing measurement is already feasible without new instrumentation:**
  `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` runs headless per-level and full-campaign simulations
  and reports `durationSeconds` / `ticksSimulated`, so a ring's play time can be
  measured against the bot rather than guessed.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Hangar economy, defence resolver and
  frontier clock are pure modules consumed by both the game and a
  `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` scene; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`,
  and `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` rejects a duplicated helper body.
- **No backend, `localStorage` only** (GDD §6.6), behind an injectable store so
  a future backend can replace it.
- **The shipped run must not regress:** six shared loadout slots, Extra Life,
  Mystery UFO, checkpoint Continue, leaderboard and settings all keep working
  unchanged.
- **One versioned key for hangar + ring**, so a defence result can never be
  written without the hangar state it depends on; a partial ring is never
  discarded.
- **Warehouse rules:** agent-initiated test runs go through `/skill:test`;
  `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill and is not edited here.
- **Documentation of record:** GDD §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (build
  status), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and `README.md`.

## Clarifications and assumptions (intake, 2026-10-30)

Three scope decisions were **answered by the producer on 2026-10-30** and are
recorded in the Appendix: **Q1 = a** (additive Hangar War menu entry, Play Game
unchanged), **Q2 = a** (ring secured = all six hexes held; the hangar assault
and hangar-falls lose state deferred to AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK) and **Q3 = a**
(ring 2 playable with generated hex definitions and headless timing). Nothing
else in the brief is ambiguous; the following assumptions are recorded rather
than asked:

- **A1 — Timing method (assumption).** AC7's "measured against the bot where
  feasible" resolves to the existing headless eval arena
  (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`), summing deployment durations for a ring rather than
  adding new instrumentation.
- **A2 — Aggression → difficulty (assumption).** A hex's aggression selects or
  perturbs a row of `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing scaling
  modules; no second difficulty system is introduced.
- **A3 — Intel is static-per-hex (assumption).** Boss identity, weaknesses and
  granted weapon are properties of the hex definition, so they are readable
  without a run and need no scouting system.
- **A4 — Defence report is post-tick, not live (assumption).** The report is
  generated from the resolver's per-tick output; no battle simulation, and the
  defending bot is never flown (design of record).
- **A5 — Ring content authoring is data, not scenes (assumption).** Hex
  definitions (coordinates, boss, grant, aggression, ring membership) are CSV
  or JSON data under `src/data/`, matching the existing CSV-seed pattern, so
  ring 2 is a data change plus generator support.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `hangar`, `salvage`, `hex`, `faction`, `outer loop`, `loadout`, `hull`
and `persistence`. The only overlapping items are the **completed design
deliverables** (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC, AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR,
AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7) which this item builds on — no completed or open item
implements any hangar, ring, defence resolver or frontier clock, so there is no
duplicate to close or trim.

## Additional risks (intake review)

- **Risk — scope creep into the post-MVP backlog** (special missions, upgraded
  bots with skills, hex personalities, contracts, ring landmarks): all are out of
  scope here; capture them as `discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE` items rather
  than growing this build.
- **Risk — two new gym scenes drift from the game:** mitigation is the parity
  guard trio (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md` rows, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`,
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`), not review discipline alone.
- **Risk — a “hangar war” mode quietly forks the run:** mitigation: the
  deployment uses `PlayScene`/shared core with only aggression-driven inputs,
  and the equivalence test rejects a copied helper body.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7** – Add Candidate D (Hangar War) and the discovery-progression rules to the outer-loop candidates document (completed)
- **AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC** – We need an outer loop (completed)
- **AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR** – Author the three outer-loop candidate outlines, comparison and recommendation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, accrual, add, adjustments, again (+385 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvcrbtnf000dk51, 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, ac16, accrual, add (+373 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, ac16, acceptance, add, again (+326 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (intake 2026-10-30)

Recorded per the shared interview contract; no answers received yet, so each
entry is marked **OPEN QUESTION** with the agent's recommended option. This
Appendix is idempotent — a re-run updates these entries rather than adding new
ones.

- **Q1 (entry surface).** How does the player reach the hex map, and what
  happens to the shipped arcade run?
  - (a) **New top-level "Hangar War" menu entry**; Play Game stays the classic
    10-level run exactly as today; Continue applies to arcade runs only (or to
    both, stated explicitly).
  - (b) Play Game becomes the hangar-war campaign entry and the classic run is
    demoted to a secondary menu item.
  - (c) The hangar war replaces Play Game; the classic run is reachable only
    from the dev gym index.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — additive entry keeps the shipped run (and its
    checkpoint/leaderboard semantics) untouched, matches the design's "the run
    is unchanged" claim, and is the smallest blast radius.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — a new top-level **Hangar War** menu
    entry; Play Game stays the classic 10-level run and Continue keeps resuming
    the arcade checkpoint. Source: interactive reply, session
    `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`; recorded as AC13 and in *Scope*.
- **Q2 (ring win / hangar lose in MVP).** Candidate D's *States* section
  defines a ring win as "all six hexes held **and the AI's massed
  counter-attack on the hangar repelled**", and a campaign loss as "the hangar
  falls". The AC list only requires capture, defence and frontier tick. Which
  of these is MVP?
  - (a) **Ring secured = all six hexes held**; the massed hangar assault and the
    hangar-falls lose state are deferred (ring 2 simply opens).
  - (b) Add an **algorithmic hangar assault**: when the ring completes, one
    resolver pass decides win/lose from stored numbers; a loss restarts the ring
    (hangar state kept).
  - (c) Add a **scripted assault deployment** (a full run) as the ring's finale.
  - **Recommended: (b)** — it closes the win/lose loop with a pure resolver (no
    new gameplay, no stall risk) and keeps MVP's cost close to (a) while
    honouring the design's stated win state.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — the ring is secured when all six
    hexes are held; the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state
    are deferred and tracked by **AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK** (created from this
    intake). Source: interactive reply, session `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`;
    recorded in AC3 and *Out of scope*.
- **Q3 (ring 2 in this build).** AC2 wants ring growth data-driven "so ring 2
  can be 12 hexes"; AC7 names a ring-2 timing target of ≈70–100 minutes. Is ring 2
  playable in this build?
  - (a) **Ring 2 playable** — the generator emits 12 hexes with generated hex
    definitions, and its timing is measured with the headless arena.
  - (b) Ring 2 supported by the generator and unit-tested, but no authored ring-2
    content or timing validation in this build.
  - (c) Ring 2 playable plus ring 3+ locked behind a "campaign continues" placeholder.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it is the cheapest way to *prove* AC2's data-driven
    claim and AC7's ring-2 target, and generated definitions keep the content
    cost small.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — ring 2 is playable: the generator
    emits its 12 hexes from generated definitions and the ring-2 timing target is
    validated headlessly. Source: interactive reply, session
    `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`; recorded in AC2 and AC7.
- **Q4 (timing evidence).** Is headless-arena measurement sufficient evidence for
  the 40–60-minute and 70–100-minute budgets, or is a recorded human playtest
  required before sign-off?
  - Evidence: `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` already reports `durationSeconds` per
    simulated run, so the mechanism exists.
  - **Answer (assumption A1):** headless arena is sufficient for the recorded
    target; a human playtest is desirable but not a gate. Recorded as an
    assumption, not an open question.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-30 — plan session (agent `Map`)**: decomposed the epic into **15 child
  items in two shippable phases**, matching the design's shipping order ("ship it
  in B's shape first"):
  - **Phase A — hangar slice (Candidate B's MVP), shippable alone:** A1 harness +
    `GymHangar`, A2 versioned store, A3 salvage banking, A4 hangar economy, A5
    hangar scene/loadout selector, A6 Hangar War menu entry + mode separation +
    deployment, A7 end-to-end verification gate (also lands the phase-A docs).
  - **Phase B — first ring (plus ring 2):** B1 harness + `GymHexWar`, B2 hex ring
    model/generator/definitions, B3 defence resolver + frontier clock, B4 hex map
    with known-ahead intel, B5 capture cycle (hex boss, boss-granted discovery,
    defending bot, ring secured), B6 defence report + attract-mode traversal, B7
    ring timing/playstyle validation, B8 documentation of record.
  - Dependencies are wired with `wl dep add` (test/verification items first; B1
    gated behind A7 so the hangar slice is proven before the ring starts).
  - Acceptance-criteria coverage verified with the shared tree-coverage review:
    **100 % of the 13 epic ACs covered**, no conflicts.
  - No new questions were needed beyond the answers already recorded at intake.

### Appendix: plan decisions (2026-10-30)

No interview round was required — the three scope questions were answered by the
producer on 2026-10-30 (Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a, recorded above) and intake's
assumptions A1–A5 remain valid. The following planning decisions are recorded so
the decomposition is auditable; none changes scope.

- **D1 — two shippable phases, in the design's order.** Phase A is Candidate B's
  MVP (a complete outer loop on its own); Phase B adds the first ring and ring 2.
  Matches `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` *Recommendation* ("Ship it in B's shape
  first … if the ring disappoints, B stands alone").
- **D2 — test/verification items come first.** A1 and B1 land fixtures, fakes and
  the gym scenes (with tests) before economy/ring code; A7 and B7 are explicit
  verification gates. Every implementation item also writes its tests first.
- **D3 — no new gameplay code paths for grants.** A hangar starting weapon and a
  hex boss's granted weapon are config variants on the shipped weapon/boss paths,
  so the parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) stays green.
- **D4 — documentation per phase.** A7 publishes the hangar-slice specification
  (so phase A is a vertical slice through code, tests and docs); B8 publishes the
  ring specification and refreshes the parity/build-status docs.
- **D5 — ring 2 is generated, not authored.** B2 emits ring 2's 12 hexes from the
  same definitions as ring 1 (Q3 = a); no ring-3 content is authored.
- **OPEN QUESTION: none.** Nothing in the plan requires a producer decision before
  implementation starts.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` is documented to validate **changed scope only** for fast iteration, but in this repository every finish gate logs:

```
WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable in <worktree> (no dev baseline, no changed tests, custom suiteCommands, or node-only selection) — falling back to full scope.
```

and then runs the **full** Vitest suite.

Root cause (read-only inspection of `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `_run_resolved_suite`): the changed-scope chain is

1. named group from changed files (`.pi/test-config.json` groups) — this repo declares none, so it returns None;
2. `_run_changed_scope_pytest` — pytest-specific, returns None for a Vitest project;
3. fallback: full suite.

## Impact

Every child implementation in this repository pays a full-suite gate. With several epic drives running concurrently on one host (observed: 5 AI_Hell drives at once, load ~28 on 16 cores) the `implement finish` gates queue on the host-wide test-slot semaphore for 1–2 h and then fail with `slot_contention` (`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600` default). Observed during AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA: three child sessions exhausted their `--child-timeout` while merely waiting for a slot, and `drive` then reset the child worktrees, discarding WIP.

## Suggested approach (either)

- **A. Repo-level:** declare `groups` in `.pi/test-config.json` mapping source paths → Vitest `--project`/`--type` groups so step 1 selects a subset; verify a finish gate logs "selected group" instead of the fallback warning.
- **B. Skill-level:** add a Vitest (node) changed-file → test-file selector alongside the pytest one so step 2 works for node projects (affects every node repo, not just this one).

Record the chosen option and measure: before/after wall-clock time of `implement.py finish` on a single-file change, and that the full suite still runs at the dev-push pre-push hook (unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A single-file change in this repository makes `implement.py finish` run a **subset** of the suite; the fallback warning is gone from the finish log.
- **AC2:** The gate output names the selected group/tests, and a deliberately failing affected test still fails the gate.
- **AC3:** Behaviour for projects without group configuration is unchanged (existing `_run_resolved_suite` / `run_tests` tests pass).
- **AC4:** Docs updated (`docs/dev/` implement/test-skill reference) describing the selection order for node projects.
- **AC5:** Measured wall-clock improvement recorded in a comment on this item.
